about.title: Costa Mesa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Costa Mesa sits where SR-55 winds down toward the coast, and a lot of the city's traffic funnels through a handful of arterials on the way there. Public records for 2025 list 619 injury collisions across the city, 847 people hurt, and 4 lives lost. Newport Boulevard and Harbor Boulevard carry the largest share of reported crashes, followed by the southbound and northbound sides of SR-55. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. are when reports cluster. If one of those numbers is you, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the crash itself. LawProactive exists to take one task off your list: finding an independent personal injury attorney who handles Orange County car accident claims. The service is free. We are not a law firm, and we do not represent you. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file in most cases, and far less if a public agency is involved, so an early conversation matters.

whyChoose.title: Why Costa Mesa Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines That Sneak Up
items.desc: California's two-year filing window shrinks to as little as six months when a city, county, or state vehicle is involved. An attorney can sort out which clock applies to your crash before it runs out.

items.title: Partly at Fault? You Still Have a Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being assigned a share of the blame reduces your recovery rather than erasing it. That distinction matters when the other insurer tries to pin the crash on you.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Network attorneys work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery. And because California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car crash cases, the full picture of what you went through can be part of the claim.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement about my crash on Newport Boulevard. Should I give one?
items.answer: You're not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and it's generally wise not to. Adjusters are trained to ask questions in ways that can shrink your claim later. Politely decline, write down what you remember while it's fresh, and let an attorney handle those conversations.

items.question: What should I save after a car accident in Costa Mesa?
items.answer: Keep everything: photos of the vehicles and the scene, the police report number, medical records, receipts, and the names of anyone who saw what happened. If your crash was near a business on Harbor Boulevard or another busy street, nearby cameras may have footage, but that video is often overwritten within days. Acting quickly helps preserve it.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything, and are you the ones who represent me?
items.answer: LawProactive is free to use, and we are not a law firm. We connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Orange County car accident cases. That attorney, not LawProactive, represents you, and they work on contingency, so you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery.
